result:
Done. Git Credential Manager is now configured globally on your machine. Here's how it works:

- **First push**: When you push to your internal remote for the first time, Git will prompt you for credentials once
- **Cached**: Git Credential Manager securely stores them in Windows Credential Manager
- **Future pushes**: No more prompts—it uses the cached credentials automatically

When you add your internal remote (e.g., `git remote add origin https://...`), the system is ready to go. On the first push, enter your credentials, and you're set.

If you're using SSH instead (which avoids passwords entirely), let me know and I can set up SSH keys instead.
